585.white: The turning of the seasons changes the color and scent of this Pokémon’s fur. People use it to mark the seasons.

586.black: They migrate according to the seasons. People can tell the season by looking at Sawsbuck’s horns.
586.white: The plants growing on its horns change according to the season. The leaders of the herd possess magnificent horns.

587.black: The energy made in its cheeks’ electric pouches is stored inside its membrane and released while it is gliding.
587.white: They live on treetops and glide using the inside of a cape-like membrane while discharging electricity.

588.white: When they feel threatened, they spit an acidic liquid to drive attackers away. This Pokémon targets Shelmet.

589.white: These Pokémon evolve by wearing the shell covering of a Shelmet. The steel armor protects their whole body.

590.white: For some reason, this Pokémon resembles a Poké Ball. They release poison spores to repel those who try to catch them.

591.black: It lures prey close by dancing and waving its arm caps, which resemble Poké Balls, in a swaying motion.
591.white: They show off their Poké Ball caps to lure prey, but very few Pokémon are fooled by this.

592.black: With its thin, veil-like arms wrapped around the body of its opponent, it sinks to the ocean floor.
592.white: They paralyze prey with poison, then drag them down to their lairs, five miles below the surface.

593.black: The fate of the ships and crew that wander into Jellicent’s habitat: all sunken, all lost, all vanished.
593.white: They propel themselves by expelling absorbed seawater from their bodies. Their favorite food is life energy.

594.black: The special membrane enveloping Alomomola has the ability to heal wounds.
594.white: Floating in the open sea is how they live. When they find a wounded Pokémon, they embrace it and bring it to shore.

595.black: Joltik that live in cities have learned a technique for sucking electricity from the outlets in houses.
595.white: They attach themselves to large-bodied Pokémon and absorb static electricity, which they store in an electric pouch.

596.black: When attacked, they create an electric barrier by spitting out many electrically charged threads.
596.white: They employ an electrically charged web to trap their prey. While it is immobilized by shock, they leisurely consume it.

597.white: They stick their spikes into cave walls and absorb the minerals they find in the rock.

598.white: They attach themselves to cave ceilings, firing steel spikes at targets passing beneath them.

599.black: The two minigears that mesh together are predetermined. Each will rebound from other minigears without meshing.
599.white: Interlocking two bodies and spinning around generates the energy they need to live.

600.black: By changing the direction in which it rotates, it communicates its feelings to others. When angry, it rotates faster.
600.white: Spinning minigears are rotated at high speed and repeatedly fired away. It is dangerous if the gears don’t return.

601.black: Its red core functions as an energy tank. It fires the charged energy through its spikes into an area.
601.white: The gear with the red core is rotated at high speed for a rapid energy charge.

602.black: While one alone doesn’t have much power, a chain of many Tynamo can be as powerful as lightning.
602.white: These Pokémon move in schools. They have an electricity-generating organ, so they discharge electricity if in danger.

603.black: They coil around foes and shock them with electricity-generating organs that seem simply to be circular patterns.
603.white: These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.

604.black: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.
604.white: With their sucker mouths, they suck in prey. Then they use their fangs to shock the prey with electricity.

605.black: It uses its strong psychic power to squeeze its opponent’s brain, causing unendurable headaches.
605.white: This Pokémon had never been seen until it appeared from far in the desert 50 years ago.

606.black: It can manipulate an opponent’s memory. Apparently, it communicates by flashing its three different-colored fingers.
606.white: It uses psychic power to control an opponent’s brain and tamper with its memories.

607.black: Litwick shines a light that absorbs the life energy of people and Pokémon, which becomes the fuel that it burns.
607.white: While shining a light and pretending to be a guide, it leeches off the life force of any who follow it.

608.black: This ominous Pokémon is feared. Through cities it wanders, searching for the spirits of the fallen.
608.white: It arrives near the moment of death and steals spirit from the body.

609.black: It absorbs a spirit, which it then burns. By waving the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a hypnotic trance.
609.white: Being consumed in Chandelure’s flame burns up the spirit, leaving the body behind.

610.white: They mark their territory by leaving gashes in trees with their tusks. If a tusk breaks, a new one grows in quickly.

611.black: Since a broken tusk will not grow back, they diligently sharpen their tusks on river rocks after they’ve been fighting.
611.white: Their tusks can shatter rocks. Territory battles between Fraxure can be intensely violent.

612.black: They are kind but can be relentless when defending territory. They challenge foes with tusks that can cut steel.
612.white: Their sturdy tusks will stay sharp even if used to cut steel beams. These Pokémon are covered in hard armor.

613.black: When it is not feeling well, its mucus gets watery and the power of its Ice-type moves decreases.
613.white: Its nose is always running. It sniffs the snot back up because the mucus provides the raw material for its moves.

614.black: It can make its breath freeze at will. Very able in the water, it swims around in northern seas and catches prey.
614.white: It freezes its breath to create fangs and claws of ice to fight with. Cold northern areas are its habitat.

615.black: When its body temperature goes up, it turns into steam and vanishes. When its temperature lowers, it returns to ice.
615.white: They are born in snow clouds. They use chains made of ice crystals to capture prey.

616.black: When attacked, it defends itself by closing the lid of its shell. It can spit a sticky, poisonous liquid.
616.white: It evolves when bathed in an electric-like energy along with Karrablast. The reason is still unknown.

617.black: When its body dries out, it weakens. So, to prevent dehydration, it wraps itself in many layers of thin membrane.
617.white: Having removed its heavy shell, it becomes very light and can fight with ninja-like movements.

618.black: Its skin is very hard, so it is unhurt even if stepped on by sumo wrestlers. It smiles when transmitting electricity.
618.white: It conceals itself in the mud of the seashore. Then it waits. When prey touch it, it delivers a jolt of electricity.

619.black: In fights, they dominate with onslaughts of flowing, continuous attacks. With their sharp claws, they cut enemies.
619.white: They have mastered elegant combos. As they concentrate, their battle moves become swifter and more precise.

620.black: It wields the fur on its arms like a whip. Its arm attacks come with such rapidity that they cannot even be seen.
620.white: They use the long fur on their arms as a whip to strike their opponents.

621.black: It warms its body by absorbing sunlight with its wings. When its body temperature falls, it can no longer move.
621.white: It races through narrow caves, using its sharp claws to catch prey. The skin on its face is harder than a rock.

622.black: The energy that burns inside it enables it to move, but no one has yet been able to identify this energy.
622.white: These Pokémon are thought to have been created by the science of an ancient and mysterious civilization.

623.black: It flies across the sky at Mach speeds. Removing the seal on its chest makes its internal energy go out of control.
623.white: It is said that Golurk were ordered to protect people and Pokémon by the ancient people who made them.

624.black: Blades comprise this Pokémon’s entire body. If battling dulls the blades, it sharpens them on stones by the river.
624.white: They fight at Bisharp’s command. They cling to their prey and inflict damage by sinking their blades into it.

625.black: It leads a group of Pawniard. It battles to become the boss, but will be driven from the group if it loses.
625.white: Bisharp pursues prey in the company of a large group of Pawniard. Then Bisharp finishes off the prey.

626.black: Their fluffy fur absorbs damage, even if they strike foes with a fierce headbutt.
626.white: They charge wildly and headbutt everything. Their headbutts have enough destructive force to derail a train.

627.black: They crush berries with their talons. They bravely stand up to any opponent, no matter how strong it is.
627.white: They will challenge anything, even strong opponents, without fear. Their frequent fights help them become stronger.

628.black: They fight for their friends without any thought about danger to themselves. One can carry a car while flying.
628.white: The more scars they have, the more respect these brave soldiers of the sky get from their peers.

629.black: Its wings are too tiny to allow it to fly. As the time approaches for it to evolve, it discards the bones it was wearing.
629.white: They tend to guard their posteriors with suitable bones they have found. They pursue weak Pokémon.

630.black: It makes a nest out of bones it finds. It grabs weakened prey in its talons and hauls it to its nest of bones.
630.white: Watching from the sky, they swoop to strike weakened Pokémon on the ground. They decorate themselves with bones.

631.black: It breathes through a hole in its tail while it burns with an internal fire. Durant is its prey.
631.white: Using their very hot, flame-covered tongues, they burn through Durant’s steel bodies and consume their insides.

632.black: They attack in groups, covering themselves in steel armor to protect themselves from Heatmor.
632.white: Durant dig nests in mountains. They build their complicated, interconnected tunnels into mazes.

633.black: It tends to bite everything, and it is not a picky eater. Approaching it carelessly is dangerous.
633.white: They cannot see, so they tackle and bite to learn about their surroundings. Their bodies are covered in wounds.

634.black: After it has eaten up all the food in its territory, it moves to another area. Its two heads do not get along.
634.white: Since their two heads do not get along and compete with each other for food, they always eat too much.

635.black: This brutal Pokémon travels the skies on its six wings. Anything that moves seems like a foe to it, triggering its attack.
635.white: The heads on their arms do not have brains. They use all three heads to consume and destroy everything.

636.black: This Pokémon was believed to have been born from the sun. When it evolves, its entire body is engulfed in flames.
636.white: The base of volcanoes is where they make their homes. They shoot fire from their five horns to repel attacking enemies.

637.black: When volcanic ash darkened the atmosphere, it is said that Volcarona’s fire provided a replacement for the sun.
637.white: A sea of fire engulfs the surroundings of their battles, since they use their six wings to scatter their ember scales.

638.black: This legendary Pokémon battled against humans to protect Pokémon. Its personality is calm and composed.
638.white: It has a body and heart of steel. Its glare is sufficient to make even an unruly Pokémon obey it.

639.black: This Pokémon came to the defense of Pokémon that had lost their homes in a war among humans.
639.white: Its charge is strong enough to break through a giant castle wall in one blow. This Pokémon is spoken of in legends.

640.black: This Pokémon fought humans in order to protect its friends. Legends about it continue to be passed down.
640.white: Its head sprouts horns as sharp as blades. Using whirlwind-like movements, it confounds and swiftly cuts opponents.

641.black: The lower half of its body is wrapped in a cloud of energy. It zooms through the sky at 200 mph.
641.white: Tornadus expels massive energy from its tail, causing severe storms. Its power is great enough to blow houses away.

642.black: Countless charred remains mar the landscape of places through which Thundurus has passed.
642.white: The spikes on its tail discharge immense bolts of lightning. It flies around the Unova region firing off lightning bolts.

643.black: This Pokémon appears in legends. It sends flames into the air from its tail, burning up everything around it.
643.white: When Reshiram’s tail flares, the heat energy moves the atmosphere and changes the world’s weather.

644.black: Concealing itself in lightning clouds, it flies throughout the Unova region. It creates electricity in its tail.
644.white: This Pokémon appears in legends. In its tail, it has a giant generator that creates electricity.

645.black: Lands visited by Landorus grant such bountiful crops that it has been hailed as “The Guardian of the Fields.”
645.white: The energy that comes pouring from its tail increases the nutrition in the soil, making crops grow to great size.

646.black: It generates a powerful, freezing energy inside itself, but its body became frozen when the energy leaked out.
646.white: It can produce ultracold air. Its body is frozen.

647.black: By blasting water from its hooves, it can glide across water. It excels at using leg moves while battling.
647.white: It crosses the world, running over the surfaces of oceans and rivers. It appears at scenic waterfronts.

648.black: Its melodies are sung with a special vocalization method that can control the feelings of those who hear it.
648.white: Many famous songs have been inspired by the melodies that Meloetta plays.

649.black: Over 300 million years ago, it was feared as the strongest of hunters. It has been modified by Team Plasma.
649.white: This ancient bug Pokémon was altered by Team Plasma. They upgraded the cannon on its back.
